annotations.text:
TODAY, IN TWO ORDERS

The ledger is the screen; the switch is the only thing that changes. Thirstiest first with never-logged above it is the default and what you land on; By place cuts the same list into rooms with Collection's drawer labels.

One rule runs through both, and it is Collection's: whatever the list is grouped by never repeats itself inside a row. Sorted thirstiest the row carries the place; grouped by place it carries the species. That is the whole difference — no second component, no second screen.

MID-ROUND

The same screen, halfway through a watering round. A plant that has had water today shows a mark instead of a figure — read out of the log, never written from here.

Nothing is lifted out and no count changes: Woonkamer still says 5. A watered plant sinks to the foot of its own room only because it is now on nought days, which is the sort the screen already does.

DESKTOP

Rhythm is gone. What is left is the plant, where it stands, the day it last had water, and how long ago that was.

Place is a column only in this order. Switch to By place and it moves into the drawer label and the column drops — the same trade the table already makes on Collection.

Below: the pieces the screen is assembled from, and the two states it has to answer for. Every value is lifted from src/styles.css and the shipped components — the row is Collection's PlantRow, the day count is primitives.tsx, the chips are Chip.tsx, the tab bar is the Collection redesign's.
